positions.as_written: Identify the target and plan the approach before the needle is introduced.
Keep the needle in the plane of the beam, because a needle out of plane appears as a dot rather than a line.
Avoid the vessels and nerves on the planned path, which is why the pre-scan matters.
Record the confirmation of correct placement rather than only the approach.
At decision level guidance matters most where the target is small, deep or next to something that must be avoided.
The defensible position is that guidance should be used where the target is small or hazardous, and that the imaging claim stops at placement.
